content: 1. A total of 24 individuals underwent HCV antibody testing, of which 15 tested positive. Among these, 21 individuals were further tested for HCV RNA, with 12 testing positive. Three individuals underwent post-RNA assessment, and all three were positive. 2. A total of 55 individuals underwent HCV RNA testing, with 40 testing positive. Among these, 39 individuals underwent post-RNA assessment, with 26 testing positive. Sixteen individuals were linked to care, and 14 of these started treatment. 3. Post-RNA assessment was conducted in 57 individuals, with 42 testing positive. Among these, 37 individuals were linked to care, and 24 started treatment. Twenty individuals underwent sustained virological response (SVR12) testing, with 18 achieving SVR12. 4. Linkage to care was achieved in 35 individuals, with 21 being successfully linked. Among these, 32 individuals started treatment, with 18 initiating therapy. Three individuals underwent SVR12 testing, and all three achieved SVR12. 5. A total of 44 individuals started treatment, with 29 completing therapy. Among these, 27 individuals underwent SVR12 testing, with 14 achieving SVR12. Seventeen individuals underwent SVR12 testing, with 15 achieving SVR12. 6. Sustained virological response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12) was assessed in 13 individuals, with 11 achieving SVR12. Among these, 2 individuals underwent SVR12 testing, and both achieved SVR12. Eleven individuals underwent SVR12 testing, with 9 achieving SVR12. 7. Data on cascade turnaround time was available for 47 individuals, with 30 completing the cascade. Among these, 27 individuals were from lowand middle-income countries (LMICs) as classified by the World Bank in 2021. These countries included Cambodia, Georgia, India, Myanmar, Nigeria, and Pakistan. Thirteen individuals from LMICs completed the cascade. 8. Sustained virological response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12) is defined as the absence of detectable HCV RNA in the blood 12 weeks after completing antiviral therapy. 9. Reflex testing strategies were compared in a meta-analysis, which included data from 55 study arms involving 88,388 participants. Reflex testing was associated with a high uptake of RNA testing (>90%, and possibly >95%), as well as improved linkage to care and treatment initiation compared to non-reflex testing. 10. The meta-analysis also compared lab-based reflex testing to non-reflex testing in terms of RNA testing uptake, linkage to care, and treatment initiation. Lab-based reflex testing demonstrated superior outcomes in all three parameters. 11. Observational studies included 35 study arms with 6,010 participants and 44 study arms with 61,395 participants. RNA testing was upgraded for its large effect size, as evidenced by the high proportion of patients undergoing reflex testing who proceeded to viral load testing. 12. Figures 5a-c from the meta-analysis illustrate the relative risks associated with lab-based reflex testing versus non-reflex testing for RNA testing uptake, linkage to care, and treatment initiation.
